Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've put together a compact FAQ below (and attached a two-column matrix + short PDF). This is intended for quick internal sharing; happy to expand into formal SOC-ready wording if you need.

Compact FAQ (what Redwood stores by default):

1) User request text (prompts / inputs)
- Default: captured. We store the raw request payload associated with the API call.
- Purpose: troubleshooting, billing, safety/eval.
- Retention: default hosted retention window is 45 days for requests; can be shortened via tenant config or private deployments.
- Example: customer sends "Summarize this doc" + PDF link -> the prompt text is stored with the request record.

2) Model-generated answers (responses/final outputs)
- Default: captured. Final model answers are stored as part of the response record.
- Streaming: while interim streamed tokens are buffered for delivery, only the final assembled output is persisted to the audit log by default.
- Retention: same default window as requests (45 days) unless the account has a different contract.
- Example: model returns a 4000-token answer; the final answer string is saved; intermediate token stream fragments are not kept beyond delivery unless explicitly enabled for debugging.

3) Streamed tokens vs final output
- Default behavior: ephemeral buffer for streaming; not persisted beyond the API call completion.
- Debugging/trace mode: if a customer enables full transcript capture, we will persist the complete stream as a transcript (explicit opt-in).

4) KV cache / session artifacts
- Default: transient only. Per-session KV (model cache) is kept in-memory/on-GPU for the lifetime of the session and is not written to durable logs.
- Persistence: we do not persist raw KV cache entries by default.

5) Uploaded attachments referenced in the request
- Default: attachments referenced in a request are stored only if the customer uploads them to Redwood for processing. If the attachment is hosted externally and only a link is provided, we keep the link in the request record but do not fetch/store the external asset by default.
- Example: PDF attached via multipart upload -> stored alongside the request and subject to same retention window. Link-only references -> only the URL is logged.

6) Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranker scores, eval results)
- Default: embeddings and other derived artifacts are stored only if the specific API call produces them and the customer's account settings allow it. Some derived artifacts are stored longer for model quality monitoring (subject to account settings and policy).

Action items and attachments:
- Attached: retention_faq_compact.pdf (one-page summary) and retention_matrix_v2.csv (examples mapping).
- If BrightBank needs shorter default retention (e.g., 7 days) or EU residency, we can propose a contract addendum or Private deployment options.

If you want, I can convert this into a single paragraph you can drop into your internal compliance FAQ.

Hi — quick clarifications to Jonas' excellent summary:

- Retention window: our hosted default was referenced as 45 days above. For accuracy: the platform default is 45 days for most request/response artifacts in the hosted plan; however, API logs relevant to billing errors and high-severity safety incidents may be retained 90 days for investigatory purposes (internal escalation only).

- Streaming tokens: we persist only the final assembled output to the durable audit log. The in-flight token buffer is ephemeral and purged at session termination. If customer opts into full transcript capture, the transcript includes the full sequence (this is opt-in and appears as an explicit boolean in account settings).

- Attachments: when attachments are uploaded to Redwood they are stored in customer-scoped blob storage and tagged to the request. They are covered by the same retention/erasure flows and can be included in bulk erasure requests. If BrightBank prefers attachments to be immediately ephemeral, we can discuss a short TTL or an integration pattern where the customer passes a pre-signed link and Redwood streams without persisting.

Adding Marissa to loop for commercial/contract options on retention TTL and residency.

Kimberly Park
